$comment: What 'deployment confidence' means, question by question, and which evidence answers each. scripts/awe-readiness.mjs derives .awe/deployment-readiness.json from this, a verify.json (profile deploy), the deployment gate and the human facts. A question is answered by suites that PASSED on the commit being assessed, never by this file. THE LIPPOLIS TARGET IS WINDOWS SERVER (LIPELE-RDS02: Node 24 + NSSM + IIS/ARR + a scheduled backup task; docs/deployment/PCC_RDS02_EXECUTION_PACKAGE.md). The container suites prove the platform-neutral application, packaging and the shared Node tools (pcc-backup, pcc-restore, pcc-verify-*). They do not prove the Windows mechanics, and every answer below says which half it covers. L3: editing this changes what 'ready' means.

questions.question: Can PCC install from a clean environment?
questions.proves: From an export carrying only repository content, the image builds from the lockfile, the preflight passes in a clean node:24 container, and PCC starts with data outside the source tree. The release package (PCC-<commit>.zip) is complete and loads its own scripts.
questions.does_not_prove: The Windows install from the zip: Node 24 MSI, NSSM service registration, C:\ProgramData ACLs.

questions.question: Can PCC be installed twice safely?
questions.proves: Restarting, restarting with PCC_DATABASE_ALLOW_CREATE still set, destroying and recreating the container (an upgrade), and starting again lose nothing: users, vendors, jobs, request, PO number, receipt, attachments byte for byte, audit history, PO sequence position.
questions.does_not_prove: Re-running Deploy-PCCProduction.ps1 on Windows. windows-deployment checks that script's mechanics statically, from Linux.

questions.question: Can the application start after installation?
questions.proves: The packaged artifact starts, reports healthy and serves a complete purchase, on Node and in a container. A misconfigured production start refuses and writes nothing.
questions.does_not_prove: Start under NSSM as a Windows service, behind IIS/ARR, and after a reboot.

questions.question: Does expected state persist?
questions.proves: After shutdown and restart, and after container recreation, the same database is opened (not recreated) and every record survives.
questions.does_not_prove: Persistence across a Windows reboot at C:\ProgramData\pcc\data.

questions.question: Can backup complete?
questions.proves: pcc-backup.mjs takes a consistent online backup of a running system and verifies it. The scheduled-backup logic is a backup.
questions.does_not_prove: That the Windows scheduled task exists, runs as the right account, succeeds nightly, and writes to storage that Lippolis IT itself backs up.

questions.question: Can restore complete?
questions.proves: pcc-restore.mjs restores a backup into a fresh volume and the restored database passes verification before it is trusted.
questions.does_not_prove: Restore on the server's paths, with its service stopped, as its account.

questions.question: Does restored state match expected state?
questions.proves: A second instance on the restored data shows every fact put into the source, through the web interface, including attachments compared byte for byte, and the source was never touched.
questions.does_not_prove: The same with Lippolis's real data volume.

untested_assumptions.assumption: NSSM supervises PCC correctly: starts, stops, restarts, and exits rather than looping on a configuration refusal.
IIS with ARR proxies to the backend, then HTTPS once a certificate exists.
The scheduled backup task runs as an account that can read the live database and write the backup directory.
The backup directory is on storage Lippolis IT backs up off the machine.
Node 24's node:sqlite behaves the same on Windows Server as on Linux (WAL, file locking, paths).
The machine that builds PCC-<commit>.zip can reach the npm registry and Google Fonts (next/font fetches Geist at build time). Found 2026-10-11 when a sandboxed build failed on the font fetch.
untested_assumptions.where_proven: the build machine; not the server, which receives a built artifact

untested_assumptions.assumption: node:24-bookworm-slim at verification time behaves like the image Node 24 at install time. The container suites pull it by tag, not digest.
untested_assumptions.where_proven: partially: every deploy-profile run records the date it ran

untested_assumptions.assumption: The paper PO history entered at initialization is correct.
untested_assumptions.where_proven: a person, before the first live PO (fact po_sequence_initialized)

untested_assumptions.assumption: Mike, Rick and the foremen can complete their day in PCC on Lippolis's own browsers and network.

not_deployment_blockers.why: S1 concerns the hosted Supabase project used by the earlier time-tracking and triage work. The Lippolis PCC pilot runs on the local SQLite store, so S1 does not gate this installation. It remains an open blocker in its own right.
The supabase/migrations collision does not touch the SQLite store's schema, which PCC migrates itself on startup (deployment gate: database.migrations_ready).
